hook.en: Every real study loses people: they move, get bored, get worse or get better and stop coming. The numbers that remain may tell a very different story from the full group. Learn why missing data matter, and what honest researchers do about them.
hook.ur: Har haqeeqi study mein log kam ho jate hain: shehar badal lete hain, bore ho jate hain, bigad jate hain ya theek ho kar aana band kar dete hain. Jo numbers bachte hain woh poore group se bilkul mukhtalif kahani suna sakte hain. Seekhein ke missing data kyun ahem hai aur imaandar muhaqqiq iska kya karte hain.

goal.en: By the end, you'll tell three types of missing data (completely at random, at random, not at random), explain why drop-out can bias a trial, compare complete-case analysis, last observation carried forward and multiple imputation, and use sensitivity analysis.
goal.ur: End tak aap missing data ki teen qismein (bilkul random, random, random nahi) batayenge, samjhayenge ke drop-out trial ko kaise biased karta hai, complete-case analysis, last observation carried forward aur multiple imputation ka muqabla karenge, aur sensitivity analysis istemal karenge.

text.en: **Missing data** happen when some participants lack some outcomes. The reason matters. **Missing completely at random (MCAR)**: the missingness has nothing to do with anything, such as a lost form. **Missing at random (MAR)**: the missingness depends on things you measured, such as older patients dropping out more. **Missing not at random (MNAR)**: missingness depends on the unmeasured outcome itself, such as patients who got worse stopping attendance. MNAR is the most dangerous, and no method can fully fix it, so aim to **prevent** missing data, then analyse sensibly and test how much the conclusions depend on your assumptions.
text.ur: **Missing data** tab hota hai jab kuch shirkat karne walon ke kuch nateeje na hon. Wajah ahem hai. **Missing completely at random (MCAR)**: gayab hona kisi cheez se talluq nahi rakhta, jaise form kho jana. **Missing at random (MAR)**: gayab hona un cheezon par munhasir hai jo aap ne naapin, jaise buzurg mareez zyada chhorte hain. **Missing not at random (MNAR)**: gayab hona na-naape nateeje par hi munhasir hai, jaise bigarne wale mareez aana band kar dein. MNAR sab se khatarnak hai, aur koi tareeqa isay poori tarah theek nahi kar sakta, isliye missing data ko **rokne** ka maqsad rakhein, phir samajhdari se tajziya karein aur jaanchein ke nateeje aap ke assumptions par kitne munhasir hain.

text.en: Think of **a class test where some students are absent**. If the absentees are random, the average of those present is fair. If the weakest students stay home on test day, the average of those present is flattered. Drop-out is exactly that: if the patients who leave are different, the people left behind do not represent the whole group.
text.ur: **Aisi class ka test jis mein kuch talba ghair-hazir hon** sochein. Agar ghair-hazir log random hon to hazir logon ka average munsifana hai. Agar sab se kamzor talba test ke din ghar rahein to hazir logon ka average achha dikhta hai. Drop-out bilkul yehi hai: agar chhorne wale mareez mukhtalif hon to peechay rehne wale poore group ki numaindagi nahi karte.

rows.en: Uses only participants with full data
rows.ur: Sirf mukammal data wale shirkat karne walon ko istemal karta hai

rows.en: Loses numbers and is biased unless missingness is random
rows.ur: Numbers khota hai aur missingness random na ho to biased

rows.en: Copies the last known value forward
rows.ur: Aakhri maloom value aage copy karta hai

rows.en: Assumes no change after drop-out, which is rarely true and can mislead
rows.ur: Maanta hai drop-out ke baad koi tabdeeli nahi, jo shayad hi sach ho aur gumrah kar sakta hai

rows.en: Fills in plausible values several times using measured data, then combines the results
rows.ur: Naape gaye data se kai baar mumkina values bharta hai, phir nateeje milata hai

rows.en: Valid for MAR; needs a clear model and good predictors
rows.ur: MAR ke liye durust; saaf model aur achhe predictors chahiye

rows.en: Tests how much conclusions change under different assumptions about missing data
rows.ur: Dekhta hai ke missing data ke baare mein mukhtalif assumptions par nateeje kitne badalte hain

rows.en: Shows how fragile or robust the findings are
rows.ur: Dikhata hai ke findings kitni nazuk ya mazboot hain

question.en: In a back-pain trial, 30 percent of the control group but 10 percent of the exercise group do not return for follow-up, and those who left reported more pain at their last visit. What is the likely problem?
question.ur: Peeth dard ke trial mein control group ke 30 fisad lekin exercise group ke 10 fisad follow-up ke liye wapas nahi aate, aur jo chale gaye unhon ne aakhri visit par zyada dard bataya tha. Mumkina masla kya hai?

text.en: No problem, since randomisation fixes everything
text.ur: Koi masla nahi, kyunke randomisation sab theek kar deti hai

feedback.en: Randomisation does not protect against uneven drop-out.
feedback.ur: Randomisation ghair barabar drop-out se nahi bachati.

text.en: Informative drop-out (missing not at random): analysing only completers would flatter the control group and bias the comparison
text.ur: Maloomati drop-out (missing not at random): sirf mukammal karne walon ka tajziya control group ko achha dikhaye ga aur muqabla biased karega

feedback.en: Yes — those who left differ from those who stayed.
feedback.ur: Haan — jo chale gaye woh rukne walon se mukhtalif hain.

feedback.en: Length is not the central issue.

question.en: Why can last observation carried forward be misleading?
question.ur: Last observation carried forward gumrah kyun kar sakta hai?

text.en: It makes the sample larger than reality
text.ur: Yeh sample ko haqeeqat se bara bana deta hai

feedback.en: It adds fake precision, not new people.
feedback.ur: Yeh jhooti durusti jorta hai, naye log nahi.

text.en: It assumes the patient stays exactly the same after dropping out, which may hide further improvement or decline
text.ur: Yeh maanta hai ke drop-out ke baad mareez bilkul waisa hi rehta hai, jo aage ki behtari ya girawat chhupa sakta hai

feedback.en: Yes — it freezes the patient in time.
feedback.ur: Haan — yeh mareez ko waqt mein munjamid kar deta hai.

text.en: It always makes the treatment look worse
text.ur: Yeh hamesha ilaaj ko bura dikhata hai

feedback.ur: Yeh kisi bhi group ke haq mein ho sakta hai.

question.en: What is the best protection against missing data?
question.ur: Missing data se behtareen hifazat kya hai?

text.ur: Jo chale gaye unhein nazar-andaaz karein

feedback.ur: Unhein nazar-andaaz karna hi masla hai.

text.en: Use a more complex statistical model afterwards
text.ur: Baad mein zyada pechida shumariyati model istemal karein

feedback.en: Models cannot recover what was never collected.
feedback.ur: Model woh wapas nahi la sakte jo kabhi jama nahi hua.

text.en: Prevent it: make follow-up easy, collect contact details, use reminders and record reasons for leaving
text.ur: Is ko roken: follow-up aasaan banayein, rabte ki tafseelat lein, yaad dahaniyan istemal karein aur chorne ki wajuhaat record karein

feedback.en: Yes — good design beats clever statistics.
feedback.ur: Haan — achha design hoshiyaar shumariyat se behtar.

text.en: **Analysing only the people who finished and calling it the result.** A tidy table with 60 complete cases hides the 40 who left. Always report how many were randomised, how many were analysed, and why people left, in a flow diagram. Another trap is thinking a small amount of missing data cannot matter: even 10 percent can bias results if the missingness is related to the outcome.
text.ur: **Sirf mukammal karne walon ka tajziya kar ke usay nateeja kehna.** 60 mukammal cases ki saaf table un 40 ko chhupa deti hai jo chale gaye. Flow diagram mein hamesha batayein kitne randomise hue, kitnon ka tajziya hua, aur log kyun gaye. Ek aur jaal yeh sochna hai ke thora sa missing data asar nahi rakh sakta: agar gayab hona nateeje se juda ho to 10 fisad bhi nateeje biased kar sakta hai.

text.en: **Make coming back easy.** A phone call, a message or a home visit can keep patients in follow-up. Ask patients who stop why they left, because the answer is itself valuable data. In a small clinic, even simple notes, such as "moved away" or "pain had gone", help you judge whether the missing patients were better or worse off.
text.ur: **Wapas aana aasaan banayein.** Phone call, paigham ya ghar ki visit mareezon ko follow-up mein rakh sakti hai. Jo mareez ruk jayein un se poochhein kyun gaye, kyunke jawab khud qeemti data hai. Chhote clinic mein bhi saade notes, jaise "shehar chala gaya" ya "dard khatam ho gaya", andaza lagane mein madad karte hain ke gayab mareez behtar the ya buray.

question.en: Does "intention-to-treat" solve the missing data problem?
question.ur: Kya "intention-to-treat" missing data ka masla hal kar deta hai?

answer.en: Not by itself. Intention-to-treat keeps everyone in their randomised group, but you still need outcome data for them. If the outcome is missing, you must either obtain it, impute it under reasonable assumptions or test sensitivity. Calling an analysis intention-to-treat while dropping people with missing outcomes is a common but misleading practice.
answer.ur: Akele nahi. Intention-to-treat sab ko unke randomised group mein rakhta hai, lekin un ke nateeje ka data phir bhi chahiye. Agar nateeja gayab ho to ya to isay hasil karna hoga, munasib assumptions ke tahet impute karna hoga ya sensitivity jaanchni hogi. Missing nateeje wale logon ko chhor kar tajziye ko intention-to-treat kehna aam lekin gumrah karne wali amal hai.

beats.patient: A trial of a home exercise programme for knee osteoarthritis randomises 100 patients. At six months, 20 of 50 in the control group and 6 of 50 in the exercise group have no follow-up data. The authors analyse only those with data and report a large benefit.
beats.assessment: The uneven drop-out (40 versus 12 percent) suggests informative missingness, so the benefit may be overstated.
beats.treatment: Readers ask for an intention-to-treat analysis with multiple imputation and a sensitivity analysis assuming that the control group's missing participants did slightly better or worse.
beats.reassess: The sensitivity analysis shows the benefit stays positive but is smaller, and the authors report the range honestly.

text.en: **Missing data can hide harm.** Patients who suffer an adverse event may be the ones who stop attending, so safety data in completers can look better than reality. Record why people left, follow up serious events, and report adverse events by randomised group, not only among completers.
text.ur: **Missing data nuqsan chhupa sakta hai.** Jin mareezon ko adverse event hota hai wohi aana band kar sakte hain, isliye mukammal karne walon mein safety ka data haqeeqat se behtar lag sakta hai. Record karein log kyun gaye, seriyas waqiyaat ka follow-up karein, aur adverse events ko randomised group ke hisaab se report karein, sirf mukammal karne walon mein nahi.

text.en: Sterne and colleagues described multiple imputation as a flexible approach for missing data under the missing-at-random assumption, but warned that it can give misleading results if the imputation model is poor or if data are not missing at random, and recommended reporting the amount and handling of missing data and sensitivity analyses. Dumville and colleagues found that many published trials reported attrition poorly and that the methods used to handle missing outcome data were often not described.
text.ur: Sterne aur saathiyon ne multiple imputation ko missing-at-random assumption ke tahet missing data ke liye lachakdar approach bataya, lekin khabardar kiya ke agar imputation model kamzor ho ya data random taur par gayab na ho to yeh gumrah nateeje de sakta hai, aur missing data ki miqdar aur sambhalne ke tareeqe aur sensitivity analyses report karne ki sifarish ki. Dumville aur saathiyon ne paya ke bohat se shaya shuda trials ne attrition ki report kamzor di aur missing nateeje ke data ko sambhalne ke tareeqe aksar bayan nahi kiye gaye.

text.en: **Prevent, Report, Impute, Test.** Prevent missing data, report it fully, impute sensibly and test the sensitivity of your conclusions.
text.ur: **Roken, Report, Impute, Test.** Missing data ko roken, mukammal report karein, samajhdari se impute karein aur nateejon ki sensitivity jaanchein.

summary.en: Drop-out can bias results, especially when people leave because of their outcome.
summary.ur: Drop-out nateejon ko biased kar sakta hai, khaaskar jab log apne nateeje ki wajah se chhorein.

summary.en: Compare methods: complete-case analysis, LOCF, multiple imputation and sensitivity analysis.
summary.ur: Tareeqon ka muqabla karein: complete-case analysis, LOCF, multiple imputation aur sensitivity analysis.

summary.en: The best protection is prevention, with full reporting of numbers and reasons.
summary.ur: Behtareen hifazat roktham hai, numbers aur wajuhaat ki mukammal report ke saath.

back.en: Missing not at random: missingness depends on the unmeasured outcome.
back.ur: Missing not at random: gayab hona na-naape nateeje par munhasir hai.

back.en: It assumes no change after drop-out.
back.ur: Yeh maanta hai ke drop-out ke baad koi tabdeeli nahi.

front.en: What does a sensitivity analysis do?

back.en: Tests how conclusions change under different assumptions.
back.ur: Dekhta hai mukhtalif assumptions par nateeje kaise badalte hain.

front.en: How can clinicians reduce missing data?
front.ur: Clinicians missing data kaise kam kar sakte hain?

back.en: Easy follow-up, reminders, contact details and recording reasons for leaving.
back.ur: Aasaan follow-up, yaad dahaniyan, rabte ki tafseelat aur chhorne ki wajuhaat likhna.
